There's not much point in me reviewing Dark Souls 3 because everyone and their mother has already said most of what can be said about the game. I'll instead focus on criticizing some things that bugged me personally.
To start off, I'd like to mention a couple of things for those curious if they have fixed some of the issues from DS2. Namely how the enemies would follow you all the time and spin around 360 degrees, not letting you get behind them. That has been fixed. One of the other issues in DS2 was ambush encounters, this game still has those BUT they're nowhere near as bad as they were in DS2. There a lot less of them and when they occur, they usually involve enemies that die in one hit or enemies that really don't do a whole lot of damage, I haven't come across an ambush encounter that was unfair.
Now, about the new issues that DS3 introduces: The biggest complaint I have is that there are enemies that have far too much health, deal a fair amount of damage and have what seems like a seven to eight hit combo without ever running out of stamina or having any kind of cooldown. These are infuriating to deal with, aren't fair at all and can drain all your stamina and sometimes health at the same time if you try to block their attacks and it's really more of a matter of luck if you'll manage to dodge their attacks. The only way I managed to deal with them is to get a weapon that can stun them and just time my attacks as they approach me. Still, these enemies aren't all *that* common, but when they show up they do make the game feel a hell of a lot more frustrating.
The second gripe I have shows up towards the end of the game (mainly) after the 'Dancer of the Boreal Valley' boss and onwards. Bosses have their attack patterns and work out as normally, but sometimes it seems like when you try to time an attack after the boss finishes his attack pattern, they'll all of a sudden have a follow-up attack taking you by surprise and catching you off gaurd. These attacks show up way too late for you to react and are especially a problem if you're using a greatsword/greataxe, because those weapons attack slowly and leave you wide open for the boss to hit you. I actually had to switch out to a faster weapon at the final boss because of how much this was a problem. This makes fighting bosses a complete crapshoot if you attack slowly.
Aside from those issues which can be dealt with, the game is pretty dang good and if you liked the previous games in the series you'll definitely enjoy this one, just keep in mind that it can be a wee bit frustrating at times.

After Spending a few months playing this game i have come to many different conclusions. I love this game!
It's beautiful and gob-smacking, the animations are fluid and quick. Areas are challenging if you don't know what you are doing and its brilliant, i just simply cannot get enough of this game. The boss's are memorable, so are the areas which  you can explore, the voice acting is amazing and the music, it's an ♥♥♥♥♥♥ for the ears. It's an absolute breathtaking game and i love it.
Although it may be an epic game and awesome to play, i do have some concerns...
My problem is invasions, and i know, i know, you're going to say "Pvp isn't suppose to be fair." and all that crap but there are genuine problems that a majority of you will agree on, I have some ideas on how it should be.
The whole point of invasions are suppose to be fun and enjoyable, but it's facing more then 2-3 people if you're the invader, okay, i can agree with that if you are desperate for help but really that many people is simply not needed, at all, the whole point of the invasion system should be to enhance the difficulty for said host, with 2-3+ people, where is the challenge? The souls series are based off challenging difficulty and with that many people there might as well be an "easy mode"... or even a "Beginner mode"
When you, the invader are faced up with them people with 3+ phantom, you got no backup you may as well crystal out. Not only that but all the people at said area and they just linger around the bonfire, with your 2-4 bodyguards with their heads up the hosts♥♥♥♥♥ Overall i can forgive all that, that's right, Invasions ain't suppose to be fair, and you should have to fight at least the host +1, maybe +2  phantom('s) (If you can play smart.), BUT, (Now this is what really gets to me!). If you kill the phantoms, the host has the power to summon them an unlimited amount of times and chooses not to fight you at all without a helper, which is unbelieveably stupid, and down right pethetic, It's really bad game design, expecialy when the host is 1) A higher level then you. 2) Has more heals then you. 3) Way more better then you at Pvp 4) has 30% more health then you. It renders the invasion system completely useless and not fun at all. DarkSouls2 was more forgiving in this matter, if that phantom died, you COULD NOT summon that same guy again untill either you died or you rested at the bonfire, yeah sure it resetted the NPC's but that was but a small price to pay for the back up you needed, and looking back, i loved that feature. Back to DarkSouls3, this time the wolf covinant, and the aldrich covinant, they are awesome don't get me wrong, but when im playing solo trying to make my way through (This has happened to me loads of times.) i get 2-3 watchdogs or aldrich faithful invade me, when you say "Invasions ain't suppose to be fair" you actualy being a hypocrite. Oh the Irony. The point of invasions is to have fun and really, it's not... In DarkSouls2 there was always the suspence of the possiblility to be invaded, you were always on edge and alert, and you needed to be prepared and DarkSouls3 takes that brilliant, brilliant mechanic, and takes a♥♥♥♥♥♥on it, then proceeds to smother that♥♥♥♥♥♥over it's face while laughing histericaly...
Overall It's a fantastic game and beautiful, it's an absolute thumbs up for me, it's not perfect but with certain fix's, it's really has the potential to be perfect. I can almost taste how perfect it would be if the invasion system wasn't as flawed.

The game is top quality, as you would expect from From. Although, in comparisson to past titles, it lacks in two major points:
1- The world: in Dark Souls 1, you were tossed into this place where you had to progress even though you had no idea where to go. You would explore, open shortcuts and realize you went back to where you were a few minutes ago, but had a new, easy way to progress. That meant the whole world was connected, and it was really what made that game so loved by its fans. Sadly, in Dark Souls 3 you just warp to the next obvious checkpoint, making going back to past areas really pointless.
2- Poise: I know this is seen as an argument from a salty fan but the poise removal really affects the way the game feels. This should be Dark Souls, not Bloodborne. In Dark Souls, you were supposed to be able to choose to be a tanky character that trades hits instead of dodging attacks, and hits hard when you land one yourself. Without poise, you don't have that option. Any fast attack cancels your own. This is bad, especially in PVP.
With that said, I still think it is a GREAT game with great atmosphere (even darker than the ones before it) and great replayability. Buy it, maybe they will patch poise :)

Fallout 4 is a bag of mixed feelings for me personally. As a Fallout game, it falls flat on it's face and hard.
However it's still a very addictive open world game and just wandering and exploring post war Boston.
They got some stuff right with it. Guns work wonderfully and it feels much better than either of the previous
iterations in the series since Bethesda took over. Power armour was the most badass thing, but the downside
to this was the damn suits were bloody everywhere. Still, the way you get into the suit just felt so proper and
how it should have been all along. Definite gold star for the badass department on that aspect. Another
downside to power armour was this new T-60, which looks almost like T-45. It's annoying because T-51 is
meant to be the best outside of the Enclave stuff and now it's not. Oh and Enclave armour is fecking
everywhere once you get to a certain level! That's supposed to be Enclave exclusive and I can find it in
pre-war ruins. God damn.
The story was like, ehh, more of the same Fallout 3 crap: find missing family member. I don't think
Bethesda's writers will ever come up with something original anymore. The forced backstory to your
character was a massive kick in the nuts, but we can thank the decision for voice acted protagonists for that
crap. Companions are enjoyable for the most part, except like 2, in my opinion. The faction stuff was bull really,
a terrible attempt to copy New Vegas and they did it so badly at that. The story is much better in Far Harbour if
you decide to get that. I really enjoyed the twists in it. Nuka World is a downgrade from that again writing wise,
but is fun if you stick it out with the raiders.
The world is well designed and fun to explore, as is to be expected in a Bethesda game. No major complaints, but
I do wish there was more greenery starting to come back into the world, way more pre established settlements
not in any way including the ones you set up. For a lot of the game it's just fricken Diamond City. But I definitely
spent a lot of time wandering and I doubt I've seen everything, even in my 227 hours. Far Harbour was great in terms
of world design. The never ending fog made it all so much more creepy and that. Really loved the hell out of it. Nuka
World was good for the most part, but a lot of empty space surrounds the main attraction with bugger all to see most
of the time. So that was a bit of a disappointment really.
The improvement in graphics is a huge step up from the last two games. It definitely makes it easier to play 4, but harder to go back to 3 and New Vegas. Although of those I'd probably only go back to Vegas and would love to get it on this
newer version of Creation, then I'd never stop playing it.
Overall it's an absolute mixed bag that I still managed to enjoy. There's a lot I left out because of spoilers or whatever, but I still enjoyed the hell out of the game enough to clock over 200 hours in it, so it ain't all bad. I'd say get it if you want, but don't expect anything as good as New Vegas for story or roleplay. If you're creative and don't mind the settlement
crap, I'd say add that to your reasons to give it a bash. If you're a real stickler on deciding, get the thing on sale.

Ultimately, I think this game has two flaws.  But, if you enjoy bethesda games - freeoform, open world adventure games, it's still very, very enjoyable.
One.  Overfocus on the settlement building system.  It's not for everyone.  I agree with a few of my friends' points when they say that it robs the game of a lot of it's personality(in terms of locales).  I like how you scavenge - it's a feeling not captured in many post-apoc games.  Others don't.
Two.  Lack of..  variety.  Lack of content?  Due to the settlement system, I'm lead to believe that this game was forced out just a bit too early.  Most of the quests are radiant, repeatable ones.  However, I've found that these mostly exist to make you explore.
This is where the game's greatest strength lies.
The environment.  The world.  Exploration.  I think that this particular world Bethesda have made, is one of their best.  It's dense and detailed, and to it's credit, a lot of those details aren't put forward in the form of quests.  It's told in the environment itself.  Through holotapes, and unmarked quests.
I haven't seen so much of this in any bethesda game.  That includes Morrowind.  Morrowind had the strongest questlines, and an amazing aesthetic design, but due to engine limitations, it couldn't tell these subtle little stories in the environment.  Due to the power of computers at the time, they couldn't produce enough fidelity to do so.
That's this game's forgotten strength.  If you'd like to know what I'm talking about, there's this excellent youtube series by Oxhorn "Fallout 4 Lore - Tragicly Beautiful Storytelling" - here's a link.
Otherwise, some people don't like the main story.  I like it, myself.
Another wonderful journey into the post apocalyptic wasteland courtesy of Bethesda. Definitely worth the cost of admission!

Edit: January 2017
I've been playing a lot of this game recently since the trailer announcing the final dlc for this game was released. I wanted to come back to it and give it another chance after not playing so long. I wanted to see if they had improved the optimization, balance, and other things I had mentioned in my original review of this game. (originally i did not recommend it for a variety of reasons, but as most of those reasons are no longer applicable, plus I find myself enjoying the games and playing a lot of it, there's no reason to keep my old negative review.) I'm still not a fan of the Firelink Shrine setup or layout, and I still think the game is a little too heavily designed with co-op in mind (Farron Keep and being dual-invaded while alone comes to mind), but overrall my major complaints with this game seem to have been polished out. I'm able to play the game and online as it is intended to be played.
In the end, as most of my complaints have been resolved, I am more than happy to recommend this game to anyone who has a rig that can handle it. Just bear in mind that there's no real dual-wielding weapons in this dark souls. If you don't mind that, and the annoyingly large firelink shrine main hub area, then you'll probably enjoy this last dark souls game. It's the largest one yet and will easily provide as much or more content, gameplay, and replay value than any of the others in the series.

I wanted to like this game. I tried really hard to like it, but I doubt i'll come back and ever finish it. there are tons of problems this game still has even after being out for a few months. I don't play it anymore and I don't know many that do still play it. In my opinion, turbophysics did a really good job of pointing out the many flaws this game still has and I would like to refrain from repeating too many of them.
Why wouldn't I recommend this game? mainly the optimization issues and the inability STILL to play online with others are big factors. but it's not even that. I don't feel a desire to play it. even alone. I played through all previous dark souls games alone and with friends and loved damn near every minute of it, but this one just isn't nearly as fun. It seems hollow, devoid of anything remarkable. It's a continuation of the dark souls franchise, but it doesn't FEEL like it. It feels like a knock off version of dark souls. I played through almost all of this one with just the standard broadsword because there wasn't enough difference between the large number of weapons in terms of attack pattern and damage.
every time I think about this game, I just get sad. It's dark souls, but not really. It feels like they kept the art style and game engine, but took out or tweaked everything that made the others great. there's nothing about dark souls 3 that makes me want to come back and play it. I wish I could more accurately describe why, but all I can come up with that turbophysics didn't already put into their review is that this game is very meh. It's just so damn meh, it's frustrating. Also, why the hell can't we duel wield anymore? Whose dumb idea was it to take that away? Not to mention armor is no longer upgradeable and has no poise. This game is dead, empty, and hollow. The things that made the others challenging have seemingly been removed-like a serious penalty for dying. No longer will you lose up to half your max health-instead, now you have embers to boost your maximum health and allow you to summon people. You get your ember restored with every boss fight you win plus one for every boss you beat as a summon and there's a ridiculous amount of bonfires now.
The whole firelink shrine area seems out of place and frustrating. Majula from ds2 wasn't that bad, but they've increased the size of your "safe zone" area where all the merchants hang out so that you spend an annoying amount of time walking around to the various merchants to upgrade your gear and buy new gear. I also don't like that you can get pinned into corners by a swarm of enemies with no chance of escape. The entire game seems to be designed with co-op in mind-and by that I mean, that there are SO many enemies and they're so much faster and stronger than you in some places, that you can't take them all on alone unless you aggro them one at a time. It was like that in ds2, but not nearly this bad-only in certain areas. It probably wouldn't have been as bad if I had been able to summon anyone or be summoned. Again, I played almost the whole thing by myself. I managed somehow to summon someone for 1 single boss fight, and that person just kinda glitch floated around without any animations, and murdered the boss without me aggroing it. I just stood in the entrance and they floated around smacking the boss until it was dead. That boss was the abyss watchers fight. I did nothing for that whole battle.
I don't even like the mana bar and the mana based estus that you can use instead of for healing. It seems like an unnecessary addition. Especially considering how meh casting is in this one. You might be able to make a caster character, but I don't think you'll go far without a posse of summons to take the aggro of the monsters away from you so that you can have the time and space you need to cast spells now. Casting magic doesn't feel as fluid or powerful in this game. the whole game feels like a stripped down version of dark souls meant to help unskilled gamers get introduced into the dark souls genre. It's somehow the easiest and most difficult version of dark souls to date and it just doesn't work well in my opinion.
I just....I just want it to be better. Fix the optimization issues and redesign almost the entire game like scholar of the first sin was a redo of ds2, and maybe I might like it more. But if the game is going to stay the way it is, I will not be coming back to play it anymore. Regardless of the dlc they might put out. (and by the way, I seriously hope they're not planning to release any DLC until they actually finish making the core game first.)
Such a pity that Bethesda turned out like this.

Get this game. Get this game, play alone, play with a friend, but don't miss out. Die, respawn, die again, and again, and again until you win. This is what Dark Souls was meant to be.

Dark Souls III feels like a mirage in a desert after the monotone emptiness of single player games that might be open, beautiful, and immersive with both a great story and great gameplay. Unfortunately, their story always ends. Just like the anti-climax after completing a great book. It’s a certain sadness over such a loss, but also an emptiness because of what used to give you entertainment no longer does. It was just a story you got told or told yourself, and when it is done, it’s DONE.
This is where Dark Souls III differs. It is not just one story, it’s many, and how many and how they end is up to you. It incorporates an ambiguous story with a dark and adrenaline pumping, nerve wrecking, angst for what you are going to face around the next corner. All the while the feeling that you must avoid dying because of what you might lose. Now here comes what makes Dark Souls III REALLY unique. You can do all this while sharing it with friends and foes that join you or you join, or that invade you, or maybe you are the one invading, hunting down others for their precious embers?
Whatever path you choose, you will end up with many stories and a strong sense of accomplishment. Some stories will be made while alone, others can be shared with strangers and maybe with friends communicated only via a few gestures that cover the most basic emotions. You will affect other people and other people will affect as you travel across this strange and brutal land. You will die, and if you stick around you will learn to deal with it, most likely grow on a more personal level.
For myself, I needed this game. It got everything I didn’t even know I wanted. It is a perfect 10. And if I were to recommend only one game, this would be it.

Now onward to the review.
It's Dark Souls, what more can you ask for?
It's a HUGE improvement from Dark Souls 2, which had problems, but wasn't terrible anyway.
There are complains, that DS3 feels similar to the first Dark Souls, resulting in people comparing the two.
Being a Souls fan, I myself felt the similarity. But nonetheless, that is what actually makes it good.
The original director of the Souls game, Hidetaka Miyazaki, returned to direct this third installment to the series, and he knew what made the first one so good. So there are bound to be similarities, although it is too much similar at certain places.
The game is still different in certain places as well, especially the combat system. It's much faster than the first one, and they introduced "Weapon Arts". This makes the gameplay better, but may be a turnoff for some.
Multiplayer has been improved tremendously, with the introduction of password matchmaking. Password matchmaking also removes level restriction, but still balances your teammate's level to yours. Which is good. The game also added more
Covenants ingame, which can result up to 8 player chaotic PvP invasion. Whole lotta fun.
Enemies design-wise, tons of new ones are introduced, while still having some similar mob enemies.
The bosses, are a blessing and a curse, unlike DS2, which is only a curse.
In DS2, most of the bosses are just "Big dudes in big armor". Lazy design, and not so smart attack patterns, which made them easy to handle.
In DS3, it is a blessing because their design is terrific and varies throughout the whole game. It is also both a curse and a blessing, because their difficulty has been amped up, but also provides a challenge.
The soundtrack is terrific, suiting the gothic theme and fantasy theme, albeit the soundtrack only plays during boss fights.
Overall, great game. It has problems, especially HACKERS. That has been resolved, maybe. I don't know. And there are tons of weapons that are unbalanced or is utterly useless. Also bugs, of course there are bugs. But they are releasing updates fixing those problems quite often.
Here's hoping the DLC to be a good one.

I, like many others, was devastatingly hyped for this game and that monotonous wait before release was truly a labour of love. I'd bought a physical copy and when I couldn't IMMEDIATELY install it, I was, understandably distraught. The several hours of installation were a cacophony of fear, anticipation and fulfilment, the latter of which had only increased during my odd 37 hours of play.
Even without DLC, a Bostonian wasteland is a true spectacle and when the thriving modding community of the Nexus (and, albeit to a lesser extent,
had clasped its perverted but skilled hands around the game, an entirely new, fervent game had presented itself.
However, despite all this merit, the game was lacking in some places, more so the main story. I just simply couldn't be enthralled by this story unlike that of Skyrim or New Vegas. It had paled in comparison to the eccentricity of this world, venturing out of Diamond City and slogging through various bandit posts, engaging in firefights or stealthing around, occasionally mucking around with some... colourful... side quests was infinitely more engaging than the 'Find your Son (press 'X' to SHAUN!)' snore.
I found combat to be far easier now than in previous games, which I was displeased with (though Survivor mode would remedy that) and as such, had challenged myself to stealth only/non-violence routes (note that dialogue is delightful, and ALL character interactions should be explored, lest you miss an opportunity for a laugh) to entertain myself.
I'd found the game to run near-perfectly on my machine (which did only have a 860m) which was a pleasant surprise, with minor over-heating when playing for extended periods (though mods had severely impaired performance, even crashing the game.)
Mods are a must, because you never know when you won't have access to internet and need to relieve yourself. (It's only a body enhancer, I swear!) But, seriously, if you want a richer story made by passionate fans, better gameplay or cosmetics (NCR armour mods are a nostalgia pandering romp and the Take Cover mod makes a firefight something else entirely) ENTIRELY NEW WORLDS and the plethora of memes.
I implore you, buy this game, invest yourself and you'll be better for it. 9/10  (Thanks, Preston...)

Now onward to the review.
It's Dark Souls, what more can you ask for?
It's a HUGE improvement from Dark Souls 2, which had problems, but wasn't terrible anyway.
There are complains, that DS3 feels similar to the first Dark Souls, resulting in people comparing the two.
Being a Souls fan, I myself felt the similarity. But nonetheless, that is what actually makes it good.
The original director of the Souls game, Hidetaka Miyazaki, returned to direct this third installment to the series, and he knew what made the first one so good. So there are bound to be similarities, although it is too much similar at certain places.
The game is still different in certain places as well, especially the combat system. It's much faster than the first one, and they introduced "Weapon Arts". This makes the gameplay better, but may be a turnoff for some.
Multiplayer has been improved tremendously, with the introduction of password matchmaking. Password matchmaking also removes level restriction, but still balances your teammate's level to yours. Which is good. The game also added more
Covenants ingame, which can result up to 8 player chaotic PvP invasion. Whole lotta fun.
Enemies design-wise, tons of new ones are introduced, while still having some similar mob enemies.
The bosses, are a blessing and a curse, unlike DS2, which is only a curse.
In DS2, most of the bosses are just "Big dudes in big armor". Lazy design, and not so smart attack patterns, which made them easy to handle.
In DS3, it is a blessing because their design is terrific and varies throughout the whole game. It is also both a curse and a blessing, because their difficulty has been amped up, but also provides a challenge.
The soundtrack is terrific, suiting the gothic theme and fantasy theme, albeit the soundtrack only plays during boss fights.
Overall, great game. It has problems, especially HACKERS. That has been resolved, maybe. I don't know. And there are tons of weapons that are unbalanced or is utterly useless. Also bugs, of course there are bugs. But they are releasing updates fixing those problems quite often.
Here's hoping the DLC to be a good one.

Dialogue and speech checks sadly have been watred down where most situations lead to the same outcome no matter what you pick. The character speaking is a debatable as some prefered to imagine what their character sounded like In my case I loved this addition. Settlements have no effect on the story and is something optional to do (except for one or two quests tied into the story). The lore in most areas has also been broken in so many areas it would take to long to list them all. Saying this Fallout 4 has alot of pros and cons yet in the end bethesda owns the franchise and im glad we got something after all this waiting.

Fallout 4 is a great game with several dozens of hours of gameplay. I have about 100 hours between both Fallout 3 and New Vegas (mainly on console), but never had as much fun with them as I have with Fallout 4. Like the previous games, the world that the player inhabits is far more important to me than the story.
Clearing out raiders and super mutants are more fun than ever. Settlements and radiant missions really do make The Commonwealth feel alive. It is very possible to become attached and invested in your settlements and settlers' livelihoods. Now that guns do not fall apart, as in previous games, it is also possible to become very attached to particular weapons. In general, I feel far more immersed than in other Fallout games.
I understand why some may dislike Fallout 4, but the overall package is loaded with content. Mods, although they should not influence opinions of the base game, extend the content so much further. I can see that the game is going to maintain my interest for many hundreds of hours and that is all I ask for.

Ultimately, I think this game has two flaws.  But, if you enjoy bethesda games - freeoform, open world adventure games, it's still very, very enjoyable.
One.  Overfocus on the settlement building system.  It's not for everyone.  I agree with a few of my friends' points when they say that it robs the game of a lot of it's personality(in terms of locales).  I like how you scavenge - it's a feeling not captured in many post-apoc games.  Others don't.
Two.  Lack of..  variety.  Lack of content?  Due to the settlement system, I'm lead to believe that this game was forced out just a bit too early.  Most of the quests are radiant, repeatable ones.  However, I've found that these mostly exist to make you explore.
This is where the game's greatest strength lies.
The environment.  The world.  Exploration.  I think that this particular world Bethesda have made, is one of their best.  It's dense and detailed, and to it's credit, a lot of those details aren't put forward in the form of quests.  It's told in the environment itself.  Through holotapes, and unmarked quests.
I haven't seen so much of this in any bethesda game.  That includes Morrowind.  Morrowind had the strongest questlines, and an amazing aesthetic design, but due to engine limitations, it couldn't tell these subtle little stories in the environment.  Due to the power of computers at the time, they couldn't produce enough fidelity to do so.
That's this game's forgotten strength.  If you'd like to know what I'm talking about, there's this excellent youtube series by Oxhorn "Fallout 4 Lore - Tragicly Beautiful Storytelling" - here's a link.
Otherwise, some people don't like the main story.  I like it, myself.

An absolutely fantastic Souls game, in pretty much any way you look at it.
Insanely responsive and tight controls are back from DS1 and better than ever, taking much needed inspiration from Bloodborne. The game now feels smoother than ever as you seamlessly go from group of monsters to the next. And while I know the near instant estus healing and the ability to move while doing so is a bit of sore spot for PVP'ers at the moment, I feel like this has really helped smooth out the PVE gameplay.
The areas give that awe-inspiring feeling that you should be used to by now from Souls games; an impending doom, a wanderlust and desire to explore and, my favorite feeling, a sense of previous historical events that led to the state that the area is in. This leads into another point about how amazing the Soulsborne games are and DSIII is no different. The lore, oh my god, the lore. It's probably one of my favorite parts of these games and FROM really did a great job in this one as well. Many things that were previous unknowns in the Souls lore have been confirmed and just as many unanswered questions continue to go unanswered. The general theme of the Souls games is still here and better than ever.
Now, there are many negative opinions in the community about the PVP in DSIII, but to be completely honest, I'm perfectly okay with the way it is. I've played quite a lot of the PVP and I found that there were very few things inherent in the game itself that were not good. Whenever I died to someone, I knew that it was basically completely my fault and my fault alone. As far as weapon balancing goes, I think it's great; there are so many weapons in use that I don't think you'd have an easy time arguing that there is one weapon that is better than the rest, or even class of weapon. So, no complaints about PVP from me.
In conclusion, this game is everything I hoped for in the final Dark Souls game and it blew my mind just as many times, if not more, than the previous games in the series. I love this game and will come back to it for years to come, hopefully even decades. This series will go down in time as one of the best of all.

In the Age of Ancients the gaming world was unformed, shrouded by fog. A land of gray crags, fun video games and Everlasting Dragons. An absolutely fantastic Souls game, in pretty much any way you look at it.
Insanely responsive and tight controls are back from DS1 and better than ever, taking much needed inspiration from Bloodborne. The game now feels smoother than ever as you seamlessly go from group of monsters to the next. And while I know the near instant estus healing and the ability to move while doing so is a bit of sore spot for PVP'ers at the moment, I feel like this has really helped smooth out the PVE gameplay.
The areas give that awe-inspiring feeling that you should be used to by now from Souls games; an impending doom, a wanderlust and desire to explore and, my favorite feeling, a sense of previous historical events that led to the state that the area is in. This leads into another point about how amazing the Soulsborne games are and DSIII is no different. The lore, oh my god, the lore. It's probably one of my favorite parts of these games and FROM really did a great job in this one as well. Many things that were previous unknowns in the Souls lore have been confirmed and just as many unanswered questions continue to go unanswered. The general theme of the Souls games is still here and better than ever.
Now, there are many negative opinions in the community about the PVP in DSIII, but to be completely honest, I'm perfectly okay with the way it is. I've played quite a lot of the PVP and I found that there were very few things inherent in the game itself that were not good. Whenever I died to someone, I knew that it was basically completely my fault and my fault alone. As far as weapon balancing goes, I think it's great; there are so many weapons in use that I don't think you'd have an easy time arguing that there is one weapon that is better than the rest, or even class of weapon. So, no complaints about PVP from me.
In conclusion, this game is everything I hoped for in the final Dark Souls game and it blew my mind just as many times, if not more, than the previous games in the series. I love this game and will come back to it for years to come, hopefully even decades. This series will go down in time as one of the best of all.

This game has traits that make it the best Fallout game ever, but also has traits that make it the worst Fallout game ever.

-The story and voice acting are actually quite good.
-Companions no longer feel like lifeless shells.
-Smoothest combat of all the modern Fallout games.
-The power armor gameplay mechanics were a smart addition.
-There's finally color! Even a blue sky!
-Weather!
-Pip-Boy minigames!
-The origin story of the main character is quite engaging and sad.
-Overall the best licensed soundtrack of the series. The score is great too.
The Cons:
-While the voice actors did a great job, the main character shouldn't be voiced in a Fallout game.
-Only ever four dialogue options.
-Where are my skill and perk related dialogue options?
-A.I. pathing is maybe the worst Bethesda has implemented yet. In my experience.
-Dogmeat takes up the single companion slot.
-Certain quests will break for some players, rendering them unable to be completed.
-Settlements are a huge part of the game, yet they matter so little.
-"Another ♥♥♥♥ing settlement needs your ♥♥♥♥ing help..."
-The Season Pass isn't even close to being worth $60.
-Where the ♥♥♥♥ is the "RP" in this "RPG"?

This is by far one of my favourite games of all time, and as such I feel like I should review it. I have spent over 500 hours in every nook and cranny of the game, exploring every weapon/shield/bow, all the wepaon arts, spells, miracles, pyromancies, everything you can imagine I've tried. I bought this game expecting to love it an llive up to the hype and it did for the most part, and I did cut it some slack considering how much people were expecting but this is my impression as it has molded and aged since I first started playing. I am a heavy pvp person, but I also like pve so this might be a bit biased in that sense. Also sorry for spelling errors, I wrote this at 3 in the morning.
I bought this game and immediately started playing. I became "Ill" So I could stay home and enjoy it. I loved every second of it. It was like playing dark souls 1 (My favorite game of all) With better graphics and new areas! My my first hour I was in love. I had already enjoyed seeing all the new enemies up to the second boss. The main things that stood out to me were that they blended the mechanics from dark souls one, two, and slighlty bloodborne, beautifully. I noticed the weapon arts and I loved them! They were amazing and each weapon had a unique weapon art (Mostly) and it was a whole new world to me. Then I opened my character sheet.
I saw that the starting armor for the knight gave me very low poise. I thought that maybe because it was starting armor it wouldn't be very tanky. Nope. I equiped my lothric knight armor and gratshield (I farmed them) and saw I had pretty high poise, so I went to the starting enemies. Useless. Poise had no affect on me being staggered or not. I was extremely disapointed and I gave up my hopes of being a tank, and moved on to the next boss. By around after pontiff I noticed as I was leveling VIT and equipping heavier armor my damage intake was the same. I tested it and defense soft capped at aroound 30 (10 highger than the starting set). I eventually found Smough's set (Heaviest set in the game) And noticed that my defense was still soft capped. I equiped ring of steel protection, and I shad roughly 32 defense. This is what really upset me, they tried to make it like bloodborne in the sense that dodging was better than being tanky. The smallest weapons could stagger you, vastly reducing strength viability in PVE and PVP. I was furious. I've been strength since day 1, and I loved using heavy weapons. In dark souls 2 poise was nerfed but still viable, and defense was godly if you had the stats for heavy armor. I could destroy people with their tiny curved swords, and I looked forward to that in dark souls 3 but I was let down. They tried to make up for it with Hyper Armor (Not being staggered and taking reduced damage while attacking with heavy weapons) but it wasnt the same. They rewareded dex weapon spamming and to make it even worse they made shields unable to be punished! As long as you knew how to block it was very hard to be hit by an enemy or other player. They also morphed estus from ds1 and 2. They took the instant healing from ds1 and the ability to move while drinking from ds2 and made a monster. Without Llloyd's talismen, its near impossible to punish healing in pvp or pve. The plus side is that I was able to change my stats and upgrade a long sword. I also dislliked that Scaling was not as advertised in the equip screen. My heavy broadsword had an S scaling in strength (Highest scaling) and my club had a A, but the broadsword did more scaling damage! Meaning what they told me when I was upgrading my weapons was incorrect. This was just sloppy in my opinion. To top it off, by the end of the game I realized there was a lot of copy paste from dark souls 1. Personally I liked this since I loved DaS1 but some people might see it as fan service and unoriginal. All of this, and the fact that and the fact that the creators are catering to the more casual audience instead of the majority of returning fans just to make more sales make the game a lot less more enjoyable than what it could have beem. These are what turned me off the most, others might think they aren't that bad.
I thought the enemies and bosses in Dark souls 3 were very unique, and I enjoyed fighting them. Some spammy enemies were a pain since tanking was nerfed (RIP Haveling) but I eventually got used to timing and dodging. They made pve either 1) Timed rolling and attacking, or 2) Turtling and attacking. This is the esssence of souls games but they took it to an extreme, since if you dont do either of these 2 tactics PVE is EXTREMELY difficult. Bosses were alll new, only a few re-used, and some had very intuitive mechanics that made the fight way more exciting (Abyss watchers, Nameless king, Wolnir, etc). The last boss gave me chills and was by far my favorite fight of all the souls games because of how it related to the player.

There are a few things that made me dislike pvp very much in this game.
All of this, plus the fact that this is the last souls game. Fromsoft has gone back to ruining metalcore instead of making better souls games (Maybe bloodborne 2 but thats all I can say) so this is what were stuck with unless we go back to a previous game. The pvp gets very old very quick and the community is not helping. Creative builds and tactics are defined by gankers cosplaying and using offhand crossbows. Unique builds are punished and some of the coolest mechanics in the game are♥♥♥♥♥♥on by darkmoon blade twinsords/straight sword, greatshield of glory, offhand crossbow, and "git gud xDDD". THe game has become a cancer magnet.
I loved the fact that playing through the game to make pvp builds wasn't a chore, something dark souls 2 was. Fighting enemies is continuously rewarding, and takes a while to get old. I spent around 150 hours in it over 2 weeks and I still enjoyed playing it. The game has the replayability that dark souls 1 and demon souls had, and introduces hundreds of new enemies to fight. By the end of the game I was already looking forward to my next playthrough. The game also makes co-op very easy, and does not reward backstab/parry fishing which is a huge pro in my book.
As a returning souls fan, you will enjoy the pve while the pvp is bad to mediocre at best. For a new player, the pve may seem difficullt but you'll grow into it and pvp will seem fine. 6/10.

I found the game to be a little too easy/short honestly. I clocked in finishing the game somewhere around 27 hours (and hell there was at least an hour or so of idle time leaving the game up in there), and BELIEVE ME, I do not shy away from exploring/taking my time nor did I summon a single person to help me with the bosses in the entire playthrough. It just felt like I really breezed through it in a semi unsatisfying way. There were several bosses that didn't even manage to kill me a single time, and several more that took only one extra attempt.

, Dark Souls 1 is good, I
that game, but please make me fall in love again instead of having all these callbacks and references to a game I already played. When you're picking up weapons and armor from characters in the first game, seeing
from the first game, and revisiting areas that we've seen before you aren't really being creative at that point and are instead attempting to carry the game with cheaply implemented nostalgia bombs.

I don't understand the hate. It's a fun game with nice visuals, a hooking story and great atmosphere. Though there definitely is a difference to Fallout 3 and New Vegas in terms of gameplay. It feels more like a real first person shooter than a rpg, because you don't have to rely on V.A.T.S. (ingame targeting system) so much but more on your own skills.
The game features interesting, quirky and in some cases loveable companions (though that's nothing new to the franchise). It's nice that the option for romance has been added, though it feels kind of lacking and incomplete. There's no real romance scenes only a little flirty banter with your companions.
I've literally sunken hours into settlement building. I understand why some people might dislike this aspect of the game, because at some point it will get tedious to scavenge for junk around the wasteland to build a nice and cozy settlement, which doesn't turn out as cozy as you'd imagined it (because Bethesda doesn't want you to build a roof without holes or to clear unwanted rabble in the middle of a nice settlement area). But the settlement creation gets a lot more interesting and satisfying with mods and the workshop dlcs.
The overall storyline is great and keeps you motivated throughout the game. Though there are minor plot holes that might sour your experience. The main quests are almost always satisfying, though there are some repetitive side quests, which however don't take that much time.
So if you like playing great immersive open world rpgs with a captivating atmosphere but don't like that your ingame succes is calculated by distributed skillpoints but rather depends on your own skill, this will be definitly something for you. Grab this game during a sale and nothing could go wrong. :)

Fallout 4 was hyped to an endless amount, but once people finished the main story, they realized that the replay value is low compared to many older Fallout Games/ES Games. Why? In my opinion it's the depth of side quests. GO play New Vegas or Skyrim. In Skyrim, a side quest can lead to you becoming a member of some guild, you gain their trust by doing varying tasks and long quests, and they seem real, they start to trust you, and you learn their secrets slowly. For example, the Companions Guild of Whiterun in Skyrim. But in Fallout 4, it seems a mile wide and an inch deep. The side quests take you along mostly linear fetch paths that end up in a non-rewarding sense.
Moreover, the DLC's are pretty♥♥♥♥♥♥ Remember the first time you played the Pitt or Mothership Zeta or Old World Blues? The only DLC in F4 I liked was Nuka Land, Far Harbor was mediocre and boring, and the rest were settlement/building DLC, and Robots with 1 quest.
In the end, Fallout 4 is fun, and well worth a buy, I feel that it would be more worth a 6/10, but I got my share of enjoyment out of it, and you most likely will too.

Pros:
- Great PVE with a good mix of gimmick bosses and genuinely hard fights.
- Most bosses are multi-stage
- A good variety of ways to engage in pvp, all of which is opt in. No more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t rat covenant invasions when you're hollow!
- A good variety of weapons are available very early on, especially if you don't mind some sequence breaking.
- Probably the best npc story lines, including ones where you are summoned to save an npc.
- A good mix of new designs and callbacks to other games in the series.
Cons:
- Most playstyles are not viable until just before or even after the pvp meta. Strength weapons are basically inferior to quality weapons, mixed damage significantly worse than single element damage, casters need close to double the stat and gear investment to come close to generic quality builds, and heavy armor is for the most part strictly worse than light armor.
- Gimmick bosses are all, with one exception, pathetically easy once you know the gimmick. The ancient dragon boss is the only one that's vaguely challenging.
- Some of the phase changing bosses are essentally two different back to back boss fights. The worst offender shall remain Nameless.
- T-pose phantoms.
Overall a great game, but it is in many ways an outlier from the rest of the series. In terms of gameplay, DkS3 draws more from Bloodborne than the other games, but also has the unique feature of weapons having a strategic impact on gameplay. To a significantly higher extent than previously, how much difficulty each area presents depends on what weapon you chose to use. A good example is the various shield knights in Lothric. If you're using a straight or great-sword with the Stance ability, they're a cakewalk. Otherwise, well, you're going to have a fun time dealing with the spear knights.
On the note of strategy, there are many times where you have to play the long game and draw enemies out, especially since enemies, and combat in general, are much faster paced than in previous installments. Sadly, while this is great in the short term, it's not helping with the replayability: Once you solve the fight, you know how to do it next time.
In a lot of ways, this applies to the bossess too. Only about half the bossess rely on good execution, the rest have some gimmick or other that you need to figure out. Once you do, the boss is just free souls on a silver platter. That said, the bosses are DO require you to just step up and git gud are amazingly made. Sadly, two of the three best bosses in the game are in secret areas that are only accessible at the last stretch of the game, so people are liable to miss them on a blind playthrough.
The othe problem with replayability is that most builds are simply not viable. You can, obviously, outskill the downsides of most of the builds, but for the most part you're better off rolling a quality build or just using the RAST until you can actually start to scale. Casters get the worst of this, with Miracles being useless until NG+, at which point they are strictly worse than Sorcery with the exception of a few buffs. Sorcery is similarly bad unless you wear a very specific set of gear to boost sorceries. Sadly, this gear is available very late into the game as well. Ironically, sorceries have the exact opposite problem of miracles: Instead of only the lategame spells being useful, only the early game ones are. Pyromancy is in a similar boat, except it gets it's necessary items 1-2 bosses earlier than sorcery, and has less of them.
PVP is the real problem area though. You may be able to outskill a boss with a worse build, but this doesn't work in PVP, especially since invaders are generally put up against hosts who have summoned. While I don't think that there is a problem with the dark sword estoc meta by itself, I do have a problem with how significant the gap in power is between those weapons and the rest.
That said, there is a phenominal amount of tools to use in PVP. Rapport, the invisibility ring, branches, and classics like the greatbows and white ring give invaders a large number of ways to trick the host, or even other phantoms. These are largely irrelevant at meta level, where basically nothing happens but fight clubs and duels, but at the mid-level meta is when these truly shine. Combined with the sheer number of ways to participate in pvp, be it mad phantom summons, area defense covenants, regular invasions or whatever else, you get a far more interesting and hectic pvp environmen than in any previous souls game.
Overall, I would recommend the game despite the obvious balance flaws, since the quality of the bossfights makes up for that for the first few playthroughs. However, I do have to caution buyers that you're far less likely to sink a large number of hours into the game unless you enjoy the more hectic free for all pvp style of lower levels, seeing as on-meta pvp is more than a bit broken.

Dark Souls 3 is more Dark Souls. With the muddling of some good features with some questionable choices, it's hard to say whether or not this sequel is "better" or "worse," but it's most certainly "more". To that end, fans of the series or of gloomy, skill-based action games will be getting more of what they love, but this game probably won't make new converts of anyone. (It is a sequel, though, so maybe that's to be expected?)
Personally, I love From Software's Souls series, and though I don't think I'll ever recapture the feeling of playing Dark Souls 1 for the first time, this game gets me close to some of those experiences. I really love the detail work in the art design, and there were multiple moments that gave me the same feelings of wonder and discovery that the best parts of Souls games can bring. There are some baffling game design choices, particularly in the area of covenants and invasions, but these don't affect my primary reasons for playing the game -- there's still plenty to discover and a lot of challenge to overcome.
Much like previous games, I'd recommend going in mostly blind for your first playthrough, with a helpful friend or forum available if you have questions. Dark Souls 3 pretty much nails the sense of discovery and ramping challenge, and it would be a shame to ruin much of that by relying on wikis, if you ask me.
After playing through the game twice, I can't really say that Dark Souls 3 is entirely innovative. There are plenty of interesting ideas and original challenges, but there are also some retreads and plenty of callbacks. There was definitely enough to keep me interested and on my toes, but I'd wished for more creativity after hearing how incredible Bloodborne (by the same company) was.
So, as I said before, Dark Souls 3 is more Dark Souls, with all that comes with it. It can at times be more of the same, but that same was really good to begin with. There are ups, there are downs, there are very pretty graphics. It could have been even better, but even an average Dark Souls game is like an average meal at your favorite restaurant -- still your favorite, though perhaps more familiar than astounding.

It's a great game on its own, but it went backwards from DSII in a lot of ways, which is extremely disappointing.
1. It has no poise, even on the heaviest armor. The slightest tap by a rusty dagger stuns you like you got hit by an UGS, which makes the most dangerous fight in the game be against three rats or dogs running into you, not an actual boss fight.
2. No powerstancing. Left hand is useless for anything except magic and shields. Left handed weapons are only usable for their weapon arts and to block with, which you would get a better effect from just two-handing it.
The exceptions are a couple of paired weapons, caestus, and the parry dagger.
3. Magic requires a massive investment, far more than melee. It has multiple items that are required to be competetive because of their massive damage buffs, and it kills diversity and style.
4. Fashion stat. With poise on armor being deactivated and defense being negligible, +equip load is basically just a stat to use prettier armor while causing you to miss out on upgrading actually useful stats.
5. Everything ♥♥♥♥ing clips through the walls. All of Archdragon Peak. Snakemen throwing axes at you from the other side of the zone and taking half your hp.
6. And, worst of all, the endless amount of multiplayer issues. Some accounts barely have working summon signs at all, and a lot can't use 4/8 of the multiplayer covenants. Then they broke save transferring and the only fix for this with it.
Still, there's lots of good things about the game, like no soul memory. Highly recommend it if you enjoyed DS1 and DS2. Just hope you win the multiplayer connectivity lottery, or you might get lonely.

This game fell short in many ways, and my ultimate outlook on it is one of relative disappointment. Flashy, pretty, and loud, its like a nineteen year old girl you meet at a rave. You shouldn't really be there, you really shouldn't be making out with her, and you really shouldn't take her home, but you do all of that anyway and ultimately wake up feeling like a moron with sixty bucks missing from your checking account.
Fallout 4 has a poorly written story with largely forgettable characters. Player agency is very forced and minimal, and early through mid game is a slog. The factions are Badguys A, Badguys B, Hyper-Liberal Goodguys C, and Obnoxious Revolutionary War Reenactors. Siding with each feels like a trivial decision which just changes where your home base ends up, and the ending is about as satisfying as watching an egg fry. The expansive and interesting environment is wasted on a lack of actual substance to the actvities in the world. Not to mention, the interface holds your hand so it's only a few steps shy of an on-rails shooter.
There are a handful of positive aspects. The character customization is substantially better than anything Bethesda has put out before, and I would like to see it return to any future RPGs they produce (this is only barely an RPG, by the way, and that's in a loose definition). Weapon modding and the voice acting were much better than in Fallout 3, doubly so in the latter category when compared to Skyrim. The same goes for the animations.
Ultimately, I can't recommend this to most people I know. For a casual gamer, it has too many moving parts and not a lot of driving force to progress the story. For avid and intense gamers, it does nothing particularly well.
If you want a satisfying experience from Fallout 4, download it, and immediately shuffle on over to the Fallout Nexus to drop twelve gigabytes worth of mods into the game that'll improve everything that Bethesda neglected to properly perform QA testing on, and you'll have something you can have a modicum of fun with.

Personally, I love From Software's Souls series, and though I don't think I'll ever recapture the feeling of playing Dark Souls 1 for the first time, this game gets me close to some of those experiences. I really love the detail work in the art design, and there were multiple moments that gave me the same feelings of wonder and discovery that the best parts of Souls games can bring. There are some baffling game design choices, particularly in the area of covenants and invasions, but these don't affect my primary reasons for playing the game -- there's still plenty to discover and a lot of challenge to overcome.
Much like previous games, I'd recommend going in mostly blind for your first playthrough, with a helpful friend or forum available if you have questions. Dark Souls 3 pretty much nails the sense of discovery and ramping challenge, and it would be a shame to ruin much of that by relying on wikis, if you ask me.
After playing through the game twice, I can't really say that Dark Souls 3 is entirely innovative. There are plenty of interesting ideas and original challenges, but there are also some retreads and plenty of callbacks. There was definitely enough to keep me interested and on my toes, but I'd wished for more creativity after hearing how incredible Bloodborne (by the same company) was.
So, as I said before, Dark Souls 3 is more Dark Souls, with all that comes with it. It can at times be more of the same, but that same was really good to begin with. There are ups, there are downs, there are very pretty graphics. It could have been even better, but even an average Dark Souls game is like an average meal at your favorite restaurant -- still your favorite, though perhaps more familiar than astounding.

I'm not going to sugarcoat this, and I'm going to be completely sincere: This is my favorite game of the saga, for many reasons, but I'm going to also say this is the game with the most launch issues.
Lets start with the pros:
-Miyazaki came back and it shows, every single map of the game is detailed, it's not boring to look at, even in places where you would be about to vomit (and there are some pretty squicky places in this game) the beauty of this world still shows.
-The music is outstanding, there's no song in this game that disappoints, that's REALLY hard, Yuka Kamitani is this time the main composer and it was a really good idea, I do think her style is better for this game.
-The bosses are amazing, even the ones that are "boring" make for an interesting challenge and the climax is one of the best I've ever seen.
-Weapon arts are a really good implementation in this game, unfortunately not dual wield like in 2, but there are dual weapons that suffice that area.
Cons:
-Balance, a LOT, 90% of the problems of this game is balance, which one didn't have those at launch however? I'd say this is only a temporary problem as patches come and go.
-NG+ devoid of change WHAT WERE YOU THINKING FROM?! Let's be honest, in 2 those changes were neat, but rather underwhelming most of the time, the extra boss soul weapons were the best change, those were really Neato... *I'm sorry*
-Poise, what do I have to give to Pickle Pee-Pump a Rum to get poise?
-Linear, I don't mean Final Halway XIII, the areas are filled with secrets and there are many shortcuts but the map is less... circular unlike the first, that had a lot of areas up and down and almost every place you could go would have a way to get to the beginning.
All in all, solid game, my favorite, the game feels a little linear (ok very linear) but every area has a TON to explore and many places to go, although 1 had really the best shortcuts. And most if not all of the problems can be fixed in future patches (even NG+ changes... what? In 2 they added a whole new ending/questline in a patch lol) I SPECIALLY want to see poise back 'cause what we have now is a mixture of "2 hits and out" and "ultimate stunlock combo", it's... it's really weird FROM POISE PLZ.
I recommend it, but if you are afraid those problems may ♥♥♥♥ your experience fine, wait till the DLCs and patches are out and then try it, but even as of now with those broken Dark Swords and Estocs and useless Dark Hands there's fun to be had (just stay away of those weapons, don't even use them lol).

This game fell short in many ways, and my ultimate outlook on it is one of relative disappointment. Flashy, pretty, and loud, its like a nineteen year old girl you meet at a rave. You shouldn't really be there, you really shouldn't be making out with her, and you really shouldn't take her home, but you do all of that anyway and ultimately wake up feeling like a moron with sixty bucks missing from your checking account.
Fallout 4 has a poorly written story with largely forgettable characters. Player agency is very forced and minimal, and early through mid game is a slog. The factions are Badguys A, Badguys B, Hyper-Liberal Goodguys C, and Obnoxious Revolutionary War Reenactors. Siding with each feels like a trivial decision which just changes where your home base ends up, and the ending is about as satisfying as watching an egg fry. The expansive and interesting environment is wasted on a lack of actual substance to the actvities in the world. Not to mention, the interface holds your hand so it's only a few steps shy of an on-rails shooter.
There are a handful of positive aspects. The character customization is substantially better than anything Bethesda has put out before, and I would like to see it return to any future RPGs they produce (this is only barely an RPG, by the way, and that's in a loose definition). Weapon modding and the voice acting were much better than in Fallout 3, doubly so in the latter category when compared to Skyrim. The same goes for the animations.
Ultimately, I can't recommend this to most people I know. For a casual gamer, it has too many moving parts and not a lot of driving force to progress the story. For avid and intense gamers, it does nothing particularly well.
If you want a satisfying experience from Fallout 4, download it, and immediately shuffle on over to the Fallout Nexus to drop twelve gigabytes worth of mods into the game that'll improve everything that Bethesda neglected to properly perform QA testing on, and you'll have something you can have a modicum of fun with.

What can I say? It's Dark Souls.
Amazing game, great gameplay, amazing graphics, good level design, great PvP; but it needs some balancing.
Dark Souls franchise is one of the best games I've ever played, to be honest, and this one doesn't fail to make you feel the usual vibe and atmosphere of a Dark Souls game. This game will keep you on your toes all the time, don't expect to be spoonfed or handwalked throughout the game, it will punish you when you fail to use your common sense to survive or when you get too greedy, but it will also reward you occasionally with items in the right times.
+The level design is amazing and punishing as always. The game puts the right enemies in the right places just to ♥♥♥♥ you up just right! What I've noticed in this one is that the levels are much much more detailed than the previous two Dark Souls games, with the better graphics and better computers we have nowadays, the developers sure took advantage of that to add as much clutter and intricate details and designs as possible, to really give you a good feel of immersion, as opposed to the empty box rooms of Dark Souls 2 for example.
+PvP is extremely fun... I've spent most of my hours on this game just fighting other players, trying out different builds and styles to make the best out of this game. It is extremely fun and rewarding, with a -mostly- great community.
+When it comes to duels. It's good to know that that From Software payed a bit exta effort into improving from the pervious games, by adding "Focus Points", which is a new bar in addition to the HP and STAM bars, which makes way for many more special moves by weapons and make the sorcery system better in my opinion. Each weapon has it's own unique "Weapon Art" which is specific to that weapon, which can only be used by the newly added FP system. *Note that some weapons share the same weapon art, but you'll rarely find more than two weapons with the same weapon art, leaving more room for uniqueness of almost each weapon.
+This one is sort of a pro, but to be honest, I always find it hard to judge, especially after putting so many hours into previous Dark Souls games, it's as if I almost got used to it, and I am no longer the scared coward who dies 5-10 times in a row from a boss because they have no clue what they're doing. The bosses are fun and challenging, although a few were underwhelming, and another few were particularly hard for me. The bosses rarely have this "Hit it's weak spot for extra damage" vibe, but they require skill and focus in order to find a good time to attack and dodge away. The best thing about this game for me is that the difficulty of each boss mostly depends on the player; a boss who you'd find extremely easy, a player could be in their 10th loading screen because of it, and vice versa.
-This is just a feeling and I do not have any cold hard evidence about it, but I just had a feeling throughout my playthrough that the levels were a bit shorter/smaller than the other Dark Souls games, but that's just my feeling.
-A few bosses were underwhelming and feel that they weren't thought out that well. One particular boss, without mentioning its name for spoilers, was a stereotypical "Hit in weakspot for extra damage" and could be killed in literally under a minute.
-The PvP is extremely fun, but requires the eventual balancing and fixing patches that come later. It's expected and justified to happen, since no amount of beta testing -closed or open- could have brought out all the potential exploits and overpowered builds that the game has. Needless to say, From Software is very active on fixing these issues, with somewhat frequent but overhauling patches being churned out since the game was released.
+Fantastic details and rich world. Every single item has it's own description, showing a little glimpse of the story of the once thriving world of the Dark Souls franchise. The game lets you discover and analyize the story on your own, leaving you to search (and trust me, you WILL find) for details all around the world, related to the stories and descriptions you hear and read throughout your gameplay.
-This might be a misjudgement since I've been playing this franchise for so long, but this game feels particularly easier than it's previous ones. Maybe it's just because I've gotten used to the Dark Souls gameplay and types of punishment that the game offers, or maybe it truly is that way, there is no way to be able to completely and fairly judge Dark Souls 3 since it will always be held up in comparison to it's older siblings, Darksouls 1 and 2. That is especially true with a lot of the apparent and nostalgic difficulty that we experienced in the previous games were a result from our own unfamillarity of the game and its mechanics, but that changed as time progerssed and as we played more and more.
I might edit/add more details to this review as time goes on, but this is all I could come up with for now. I hope this review helps you decide better whether you want to buy this game or not!

This game fell short in many ways, and my ultimate outlook on it is one of relative disappointment. Flashy, pretty, and loud, its like a nineteen year old girl you meet at a rave. You shouldn't really be there, you really shouldn't be making out with her, and you really shouldn't take her home, but you do all of that anyway and ultimately wake up feeling like a moron with sixty bucks missing from your checking account.
Fallout 4 has a poorly written story with largely forgettable characters. Player agency is very forced and minimal, and early through mid game is a slog. The factions are Badguys A, Badguys B, Hyper-Liberal Goodguys C, and Obnoxious Revolutionary War Reenactors. Siding with each feels like a trivial decision which just changes where your home base ends up, and the ending is about as satisfying as watching an egg fry. The expansive and interesting environment is wasted on a lack of actual substance to the actvities in the world. Not to mention, the interface holds your hand so it's only a few steps shy of an on-rails shooter.
There are a handful of positive aspects. The character customization is substantially better than anything Bethesda has put out before, and I would like to see it return to any future RPGs they produce (this is only barely an RPG, by the way, and that's in a loose definition). Weapon modding and the voice acting were much better than in Fallout 3, doubly so in the latter category when compared to Skyrim. The same goes for the animations.
Ultimately, I can't recommend this to most people I know. For a casual gamer, it has too many moving parts and not a lot of driving force to progress the story. For avid and intense gamers, it does nothing particularly well.
If you want a satisfying experience from Fallout 4, download it, and immediately shuffle on over to the Fallout Nexus to drop twelve gigabytes worth of mods into the game that'll improve everything that Bethesda neglected to properly perform QA testing on, and you'll have something you can have a modicum of fun with.

So first things first, if you are still Dark Souls-virgin I recommend you start off with any of the games prior to this (Dark Souls 1, Dark Souls 2 or Bloodborne).
Dark Souls 3 takes place after the events from Dark Souls 1 ignoring the events from Dark Souls 2 (I'll discuss Dark Souls 2 later on since there's some important points to be made) and takes a more Bloodborne-like combat approach instead of the one we could see in Dark Souls 1 and 2 which was slower and clunkier, in a way this is a good thing in my opnion since anyone who has played earlier installmens has died at least once due to the clunky movements of the character or our camera going crazy when you had a wall behind you, another point worth mentioning is that unlike earlier installments, Dark Souls 3 is actually playable with a mouse and keyboard, the controlls take a little to get used to but after you get the hang of them you should'nt have trouble playing the game.
Now the bad stuff, we all know that Dark Souls 2 was not a great game, in fact is considered the worst of the franchise but at least they got some things right, things that should've stayed yet they were removed, I still cannot explain why they removed the NG+ new enemy placements or the blue eye orb, but the part that annoys me the most, they brought back the most hated thing in souls games but multiplied by 3... autosummon covenants, in previous games we had the bell keepers and the forest hunters which meant only 1 autosummon covenant per game, Well in Dark Souls 3 we have 3 of them, Watchdogs of Farron, Aldrich Faithful and Blades of the Darkmoon, which at least they fixed the blades of the darkmoon but in all my playtime I have never been summoned for Watchdogs or Aldrich
So TL;DR
Pros:
+Faster gameplay
+Mouse/Kyeboard combo friendly
+Easier to connect with friends compared to other games
+More challenging gameplay (Definatelly harder than previous entries)
+Surprisingly responsive online connection
+No more soul memory
Cons:
-More autosummon covenants
-No blue eye orb
-Removal of the dual-wielding mechanic Dark Souls 2 had
-NG+ stays the same outside from the ability to get stronger rings
-Invasions prioritize players who have phantoms summoned
-The worst PVP of all games
Would I recommend the game? Hell yes
Is it game of the year material? Hell no
Overall rating: 8/10

Then here comes 3 and I have to say it was a really good return to my Dark Souls roots. The combat harkens back to the first game and with it came my love of melee combat. It is where this game shines. At first there was some rust but as I play more the instincts and skills have started to come back. I feel like I haven't missed a beat. Which is what made 2 so frustrating. It was like re learning how to walk in this new and very odd feeling mess. If you loved 1's combat this is for you. The only thing that I find lacking is the level design. In the 1st one the whole world is interconnected in multiple places. You can get to multiple places from different areas. The game is stacked vertically not laid out horizontally. 3's map is very linear. There really isn't much deviation. Just follow the path an you'll get there. The only place I found disorienting was Farrons Keep. Other than that it is really easy to find out where to go.

I have played Fallout 4 two hundred twenty-five hours and counting. I wanted to write this review well after Fallout 4 had been released, all of the DLC had been released, and when the modding community had really had a good opportunity to get a foothold in. Fallout 4 is an amazing game all in all. To those people who were giving this game 0's and 10's on the very first day it was released, within the first 10 minutes of playing, all I got to say is that those reviews don't help ANYONE. A game like this takes time to grow.
Gameplay
Gameplay probably features the biggest changes and improvements of the Fallout series. Improvements can be found from various aspects of the game, from combat, exploration, crafting and character building. Compared to Fallout 3, the combat is much more responsive, faster and dynamic. Enemy variation is amazing in Fallout 4 and it was often surprising to see new features and abilities added to already known enemy types. Crafting is one of the biggest and greatest part of Fallout 4. As soon I saw the new crafting system of Fallout 4 in E3, I knew it was going to be great and sure wasn’t disappointed. With Automatron DLC you can also build your own robots, and go far as building your own kickass Sentry Bot. With the improved crafting looting and exploration became more important and rewarding. Junk rarity was also in great balance, I often found myself missing needed materials which then motivated me go out to explore the wasteland. With the new crafting system also came the settlement mode, which allowed players to create their own towns and settlements. To me the vanilla settlement mode was dull in many ways. Either way the settlement mode can a lot of fun with mods, allowing you to actually craft something genuine and incredible. The leveling and perk system was also redesigned. While there was nothing wrong with the previous system, the new system was a welcome change.
Atmosphere
In general, the atmosphere in Fallout 4 is subtler than in previous entries. Commonwealth felt much brighter and hopeful than the desolate Capital Wasteland or Mojave Desert. This is likely due to the more vibrant weathers. To improve immersion, Bethesda did a nice job of reducing the amount of loading screens. Abandoned towns now could be explored without having to struggle through the 5 second loading screen every now and then.
Story and Quests
I personally enjoyed the main plot, mainly because I didn’t expect much of it I got what I expected. Most of the main storyline was very good, it definitely had some memorable moments, difficult choices and the total length of the story wasn’t too bad. As for side content and quests, which were usually good but often hard to find. Radiant quests in Fallout 4 have a large role. The highly criticized voiced protagonist and the new dialogue system didn’t bother me, which did undoubtedly pose problems. But to me they were welcome changes, which felt like taking one step back and two steps forward.
Overall
While Fallout 4 did sacrifice some of its predecessors RPG elements, it still turned out to be one of the best open-world shooter that I’ve played. Fallout did change for better or worse, but as for me, it’s still a Fallout game, and a damn good one.
I would give it a try if i were you ;)

I'll be breaking this review up into two sections, Single-Player and Multi-player. Although, take this review with a grain of salt due to the fact I may be favoring the earlier games, but do keep in mind the amount of time I've put into this game.
Single-Player
The Single-Player is one of the most enjoyable but frustrating experiences you'll have in gaming. The boss fights are wonderfully designed to give you a challenging but rewarding fight that makes you actually have to learn the patterns and ways the boss fights. The areas around the game give a sense of progression and allow you to see more of the world you're in. Oh yeah also, lore.
Multi-Player:
Out of these two segments I'd have to give Multi-Player a worse rating. The PvP is an utter mess at the moment due to the fact instead of using the usual "poise" system From Software has completely disabled it and instead uses a newer but less reliable "hyper armor" system, to put it simply, Greatswords Ultra Greatswords anything similar to it are unstaggerable on most of their move sets except for some exceptions but weapons such as Straight Swords are unable to get any unstaggerable frames making using a Greatsword more meta and makes a fight where its a Greatsword V.S Straight Sword horribly unbalanced and the hyper armor system could use some reworking. Beside PvP the online community is mostly helpful and people will put their signs down in-front of boss rooms if you need help just like any over souls game.
If From Software makes any positive changes to the new hyper armor system or just general PvP improvements I will edit this review and take the new changes into account.
